summary: Red Plume lookout in the Great Bear Wilderness: a 1928 cabin on the ground, a 15-foot replacement tower, destroyed in 1991. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 15-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab, replacing a 1928 D-6 cupola cabin built on the ground
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1991 per firelookout.com. No source describes what remains at the site.

access.note: Inside the Great Bear Wilderness on Flathead National Forest land. No source describes access to the old site.

events.note: D-6 cupola cabin, built on the ground per the April 1954 account. firelookout.com dates it to 1928.
The old cabin was declared unsafe for further occupancy, per the April 1954 account.
The Montana Lookouts page gives 1955 for completion of the new tower. firelookout.com gives 1957 for the 15-foot tower.
Leif Holgerson listed as a lookout, per firelookout.com.
Kenneth Thompson listed as a lookout, per firelookout.com.
Britt Franklin was a fire lookout at Red Plume, per the oral history description.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The April 1954 account says the 1928 lookout was built on the ground, which fits firelookout.com's cupola cabin label. Both describe the same original structure.
The April 1954 account and firelookout.com both give 15 feet. A September 1954 item giving 10 feet is the outlier, so the record keeps 4.6 m (15 ft).

notes_for_editor: Replacement completion: 1955 (Montana Lookouts page) against 1957 (firelookout.com). Height: 15 ft in the April 1954 account and firelookout.com; 10 ft in a September 1954 item; the record keeps 4.6 m. Elevation: 7,947 ft (firelookout.com) against 7,500 ft (1954 account). A Flathead National Forest Facebook post about the 1928 build came up in search, but fetch_text returned only its title, so it is not cited. No source found describes the site today. The 1967 staffing comes from the oral history description. The access note cites only the Forest Service wilderness page; no source describes the route to the site.
